title: Popularity Bias in Recommenders
interviewAnswer: Highly active/popular entities can dominate recommendations even when niche specialists are more relevant. Mitigation can include debiasing, re-ranking, diversity constraints or separating expertise from activity.
why: Recommenders often over-recommend popular items/users because historical interactions are heavily skewed, reducing personalization and specialist discovery.
intuition: If one maintainer reviews almost everything, the model can learn “recommend the maintainer” and score well without learning topic-specific expertise.
deepDive: Bias comes from exposure and label imbalance: popular candidates have more training edges and more chances to be selected. Mitigations include candidate normalization, degree-aware features/losses, debiasing embeddings, diversity constraints and separating expertise from activity. Improvements should be validated against relevance, not just forced equal exposure.
workedExample: Centroid subtraction can remove a generic “core team” direction so niche PR text surfaces specialists rather than the same high-degree maintainer every time.
commonMistakes: Assuming popularity is always bad—high activity may be a valid reliability signal.
Forcing equal recommendation rates regardless of relevance.
Evaluating only aggregate Recall@K and missing long-tail quality.
followUps: How would you measure popularity bias?
How do you balance expertise and activity?
production: Monitor recommendation concentration, long-tail coverage, acceptance and workload distribution. Provide business controls when activity/availability is operationally important.
